issues.issue: Whether the designated judge should have refused to hear the respondent's second application for judicial release, absent a material change of circumstances
issues.applicant_position: Ministers say no substantial change existed, and events before Lemieux J.'s December 2005 decision were wrongly considered.
issues.result_quote: In conclusion, we are satisfied that there is no merit in this first ground of appeal.

issues.issue: Whether the judge applied a stricter imminent-removal test instead of the s.84(2) reasonable-time test
issues.applicant_position: Ministers say the judge substituted imminence of removal for removal within a reasonable time.
issues.result_quote: It cannot be said that she applied the wrong test in view of what the appellants were pleading.

issues.issue: Whether the sureties and performance bonds chosen were so flawed that they defeat the release terms as a whole
issues.applicant_position: Ministers say the sureties and three bond signers were unsuitable, so the conditions do not neutralize the risk.
issues.result_quote: We are satisfied that the choice of sureties by the designated judge is not so flawed as to trump the cumulative effect of all the conditions and terms.

issues.issue: Whether the electronic monitoring limits, the geographic area and the refused Arabic-language undertaking make release unsafe
issues.applicant_position: Ministers say monitoring is unreliable, the geographic area is too broad, and the Arabic undertaking should have been accepted.
issues.result_quote: Upon the filing of the appropriate evidence, the appellants are free to go back to the designated judge to seek a variation
